record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: If a polynomial automorphism f of C^d satisfies λ(f)=1, must deg(f^n) grow like n^k for some k∈N, and if k≥1 must f preserve a rational fibration?

evidence.quote: Question 39. — Suppose f is a polynomial automorphism of Cd satisfying λ(f) = 1. Is it true that deg(fn) ≍ nk for some k ∈ N? Moreover, if k ≥ 1, does f preserve a rational fibration?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^d\to\mathbb{C}^d$ be a polynomial automorphism, i.e., a bijective polynomial map whose inverse is also polynomial. Write $f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ and define $\deg(f)=\max_{1\le i\le d}\deg(f_i)$. The first dynamical degree of $f$ is
$$\lambda(f)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\deg(f^n)^{1/n},$$
where $f^n$ denotes the $n$-fold iterate. Assume $\lambda(f)=1$.

(a) Must there exist an integer $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and constants $0<c\le C<\infty$ such that
$$c\,n^k\le \deg(f^n)\le C\,n^k\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n?$$

(b) If such a $k$ exists and $k\ge 1$, must $f$ preserve a rational fibration, i.e., must there exist a dominant rational map $\pi:\mathbb{C}^d\dashrightarrow Y$ to a positive-dimensional variety $Y$ and a rational self-map $g:Y\dashrightarrow Y$ with $\pi\circ f = g\circ\pi$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a list of open problems on Hénon-type and polynomial automorphism dynamics. In dimension 2 it is fully known (Friedland-Milnor; Favre-Jonsson), but in arbitrary dimension $d\ge 3$ the conjectured integer polynomial growth of $\deg(f^n)$ and the existence of an invariant rational fibration for $\lambda(f)=1$ remain open; recent works (e.g., Lo Bianco and others on degree growth of polynomial automorphisms) construct new examples but do not settle the general question.

status_evidence.title: Degree growth of polynomial automorphisms and birational maps: some examples
status_evidence.snippet: Provides new examples of degree growths for polynomial automorphisms of C^k with k≥3.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of possible degree growths for polynomial automorphisms in dimension ≥3 is still under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Spectral interpretations of dynamical degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses dynamical degrees of polynomial automorphisms; results are complete in dimension 2 (Friedland, Milnor, Favre, Jonsson).
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional analogues of the dimension-2 results on degree growth and invariant fibrations remain conjectural.
